body:
Splitting the unfinished half of #118 into its own issue.

#118 asked for two things: an audit to find where stock-solution concentrations and unit slips were stored as final per-litre values, and the corpus repair. **#135 shipped the audit only** — its merge commit says so outright:

> `Does NOT close #118; the corpus repair remains.`

#118 was nonetheless closed on 2026-07-26. The corpus is still wrong; what changed is that we now know exactly where. This issue tracks the repair.

## What the audit found

Three read-only detectors, output in `data/import_tracking/reports/concentration_plausibility.tsv` and `…_by_record.tsv`. Re-counted from the committed reports on 2026-07-30:

| detector | rows | signal |
|---|--:|---|
| `INDICATOR_UNIT_SLIP` | 5,601 | indicators/vitamins ≥ 0.1 G_PER_L — a ~1000x slip |
| `TRACE_SALT_AS_STOCK` | 5,341 | trace-element salts ≥ 1 G_PER_L — stock-solution magnitude |
| `WATER_AS_VOLUME` | 598 | water ≥ 1000 G_PER_L — a prep volume flattened into the ingredient list |

**11,540 rows across 3,914 records.** All three records named in #118 are detected and pinned by a regression test.

## The actionable subset

**579 records are flagged `flattened_cocktail`** — three or more flagged vitamin/trace rows *and* no `solutions:` block. For these the repair is structural ("nest this cocktail under a solution object with an addition volume") rather than per-value, which makes them both higher-value and more mechanical than the rest. The remaining 3,335 flagged records are not cocktails and need per-value judgment.

`DSMZ_962a_THERMOVENABULUM_MEDIUM` is the worked example: the entire DSMZ vitamin solution flattened into `ingredients:` at stock strength.

## Scope limits — read before trusting the counts

- **Only `G_PER_L` rows are examined** (149,289 of 166,684). `MILLIMOLAR`, `MG_PER_L` and `VARIABLE` are untouched. A molar-basis check needs molecular weights and is separate work.
- **Detectors key on confirmed failure modes, not outlier statistics**, so bulk-nutrient errors are missed. `MARICAULIS_medium` carries `Peptone 100 G_PER_L` and `Yeast extract 50 G_PER_L`, both implausible, neither flagged.
- **Stock-solution records are excluded** via `record_kinds.is_solution_record` (from #124), where high magnitudes are correct by definition. Without that exclusion this would flag thousands of the ~4,784 solution records sitting in `bacterial/`.

So 11,540 is a floor on the real defect count, not a total.

## Remaining work

1. Nest the 579 detected cocktails under stock `solution` objects with addition volumes.
2. Work the non-cocktail flagged records per value.
3. Add a plausibility validator to the schema-gap / label-plausibility harness so new imports cannot reintroduce this — the audit is currently read-only and nothing stops a fresh import landing the same shape.

Item 3 is arguably the highest-leverage: without it the corpus repair is a one-off sweep that decays.

comments.body:
## Proposal tooling added (PR #236)

`just propose-cocktail-nesting` now turns the 579 flattened cocktails into a
reviewable worklist (non-destructive — it edits nothing). Per record it lists the
flagged trace/vitamin components to nest, a **candidate** addition volume recovered
from the record's own preparation_steps/notes with its evidence sentence (or
`MANUAL`), and the proposed nested-solution shape.

Reality check on volume recovery: of 579, ~15 yield a candidate volume from the
record itself and 564 are `MANUAL`. The candidates still include false positives (a
volume next to "methanol"; a pH-adjust step), each visible in `volume_evidence` —
which is why the tool proposes rather than applies. A wrong volume corrupts the
recipe (`stock_conc x volume/1000`), so the actual nesting stays a per-record
curator step over this worklist, ideally with the upstream source (togo/DSMZ) open
for the 564 that the record itself does not pin.

Remaining on #150: the per-record application itself (a curation pass over the
worklist), which is the judgement-heavy step this tooling exists to support.

## Addition volumes are now authoritative for 180 records (PR #242)

The blocker on this repair was the per-record addition volume: #236 could only
scrape 15 candidates from record prose, several of them false positives, so the
repair stayed curator-only.

**MediaDive states the volume structurally.** `/rest/medium/{id}` returns
`solutions[]`, and a solution's recipe references another solution with the volume
it contributes:

```json
{"solution": "Wolfe's mineral elixir", "solution_id": 1605, "amount": 1, "unit": "ml"}
```

`just fetch-mediadive-volumes` pulls this for the 186 flattened cocktails that
resolve to a numeric MediaDive id; **180 get a real volume**. The worklist now reads:

| volume_source | records |
|---|--:|
| MEDIADIVE (authoritative) | 180 |
| preparation_steps/notes (prose candidate) | 6 |
| MANUAL | 393 |

Volumes are varied (1, 2, 5, 10, 0.1, 0.5, 50 ml) — not a constant that could have
been assumed.

**Verified the diagnosis end to end:** `aciduliprofundum_medium`'s flagged MnSO4 5,
FeSO4 1, CoCl2 1.8, ZnSO4 1.8 G_PER_L are *exactly* Wolfe's mineral elixir's stock
values in MediaDive, added at 1 ml into 1000 ml — the flattening overstates them
~1000x, precisely what this issue describes, now with the dilution factor available.

**Remaining:** applying the nesting per record. For the 180 MEDIADIVE records that
is now a mechanical transform with an authoritative volume (still worth applying in
reviewed batches, since it restructures real recipes). The 393 MANUAL records need a
non-MediaDive source or curator judgement; most carry KOMODO/JCM ids MediaDive does
not serve (same id-resolution wall as #239).

## Corpus repair: 135 cocktails nested (PR #243)

The repair #118 asked for and #135 deferred is now partly done — the first actual
corpus change on this issue.

| metric | before | after |
|---|--:|--:|
| implausible rows | 11,540 | **10,913** (627 repaired) |
| affected records | 3,914 | **3,782** |
| flattened cocktails | 579 | **444** (135 repaired, 23%) |

Each moved component matched the MediaDive stock by **name AND value** — the guard
that matters, because a stock's component list overlaps the medium's bulk salts
(Wolfe's elixir lists NaCl 10 g/l; `aciduliprofundum_medium` carries main-solution
NaCl 39.97, which correctly stayed put). 44 records whose flagged rows didn't all
match were skipped whole rather than half-repaired. Gate baselines tightened to
10,913 / 444.

## What remains (444)

- **~400** are media carrying KOMODO/JCM ids that MediaDive does not serve — the same
  id-resolution wall as #239. Not recoverable without resolving those ids to a source
  that publishes the stock composition and addition volume.
- **44** resolve to MediaDive but have flagged rows that did not match the stock by
  name+value. These need per-record judgement: usually a vitamin whose name differs
  from MediaDive's spelling, or a value that genuinely differs from the stock. The
  applier reports them (`just apply-cocktail-nesting`) with the unmatched names.

Both are curation work, not tooling gaps. `just apply-cocktail-nesting` is re-runnable
if more volumes become resolvable.

## Second pass: KOMODO id wall broken, 204 of 579 now repaired (PR #245)

The ~400 records I called blocked were resolvable after all. They carry
`komodo.medium:` ids, but **DSMZ medium numbers are MediaDive ids**, and the tracked
`komodo_dsmz_mappings.json` maps KOMODO -> DSMZ for all 261 KOMODO-sourced cocktails.

| metric | original | after #243 | after #245 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| implausible rows | 11,540 | 10,913 | **10,614** (926 repaired) |
| affected records | 3,914 | 3,782 | **3,716** |
| flattened cocktails | 579 | 444 | **375** (204 repaired, 35%) |

**The mapping needed a guard, and it mattered.** 43.5% of it is identity, and
MediaDive has renumbered since the snapshot, so every resolved id is now confirmed by
fetching the medium and name-checking it. Of 312 resolved records, **165 disagreed**
— KOMODO 294 "Pelobacter acidigallici" resolves to MediaDive 294 "Syntrophus HQGo1".
Each would have imported another medium's stock composition. Filed as **#244**, which
also notes some *direct* `mediadive.medium:` ids in the corpus are wrong.

## Remaining 375
- **165** have a resolvable id whose fetched medium disagrees by name — blocked on
  #244 (correct the ids), not on this repair.
- **57** resolve and match, but some flagged rows don't match the stock by
  name+value. Diagnosed: when a medium references two stocks sharing a component
  name, the flattening SUMMED them (chrysiogenes: pyridoxine 0.4 = Wolin's 0.1 +
  Seven vitamins 0.3). 11 records are pure-sum cases and could be split
  deterministically; the rest are mixed causes.
- The remainder carry JCM/TOGO ids or no resolvable id (the #239 wall, genuinely).

`just apply-cocktail-nesting` is re-runnable as #244 corrects ids.

## Third pass: summed-stock split (PR #248). 220 of 579 repaired.

| metric | original | now |
|---|--:|--:|
| implausible rows | 11,540 | **10,521** (1,019 repaired) |
| affected records | 3,914 | **3,700** |
| flattened cocktails | 579 | **359** (220 repaired, 38%) |

The 57 records refused after the KOMODO pass had a specific cause: when a medium
references TWO stocks sharing a component, the flattening **summed** them.
`chrysiogenes_medium` carries pyridoxine 0.4 = Wolin's 0.1 + Seven vitamins 0.3.
`--split-summed` restores each stock's own value, accepted only on exact sum
equality, and mass conservation (parts re-summing to the flattened value) is the
proof. 16 records recovered.

## Where the remaining 359 stand

- **165** — KOMODO ids with no trustworthy MediaDive counterpart. **Not** an id
  defect: #244 established the corpus's own ids are 100% sound; the KOMODO->DSMZ
  mapping is what misleads (~72% wrong), and only 39 of 2,605 have a unique name
  match. Genuinely blocked without a better cross-reference.
- **41** — resolve to MediaDive but have rows that neither match a stock nor
  reconcile as a sum. Mixed causes needing per-record judgement (a vitamin spelled
  differently from MediaDive's, or a value that genuinely differs).
- The remainder carry JCM/TOGO ids that publish no stock composition.

All three are curation or upstream-data limits, not tooling gaps.
`just apply-cocktail-nesting [--split-summed]` is re-runnable if better
cross-references appear.

## Edison literature lane opened for the blocked cocktails (PR #249)

Built and canaried the research path for the 315 records MediaDive cannot supply,
including the 165 blocked by the #244 KOMODO wall.

**Prompt:** `templates/media_stock_solution_research.md` asks for the two missing
facts — which named stock the stock-strength entries belong to, and its addition
volume per litre. Its key instruction is the refusal clause (report
`addition_volume_found: false` rather than infer a typical dose, #166) and a warning
against confusing the addition volume (1 ml/L) with the stock's preparation volume
(1000 ml).

**Targets:** `just list-cocktail-research-targets` lists the blocked set with the
reason each is blocked, and reports cluster structure — 104 records are variants of
28 base media ("MEDIUM 252 MODIFIED FOR DSM …" ×30), so the 165 group needs only 110
runs, not 165.

### Canary + 3-record sample (live, cost 0.0000, ~8 min each)

| record | stocks named | addition volume |
|---|--:|---|
| KOMODO_503c_PROPIONISPORA | 3 | **found — 1 mL/L each** |
| KOMODO_194_DESULFOBULBUS | 3 | not found |
| KOMODO_294_PELOBACTER | 3 | not found |
| pyrodictium_abyssi | 0 | — |

**3 of 4 named the stocks with composition; 1 of 4 gave the volume.** The canary
returned a well-reasoned negative ("A generic seven-vitamin dose such as 1 ml/L must
not be inferred"), independently confirmed #244 ("no authoritative DSMZ Medium 508
sheet was retrievable"), and found a defect I had not: several vitamins appear twice
under variant names — two overlapping flattened blocks in one record.

### A cross-check worth recording
Every stock Edison named is a standard DSMZ one, and the MediaDive data already
fetched shows how invariant their volumes are:

```
Trace element solution SL-10   36/36 at 1 ml/L  (100%)
Trace elements solution         6/6  at 10 ml/L (100%)
Seven vitamins solution        44/48 at 1 ml/L  (92%)
Vitamin solution                3/8  at 1 ml/L  (38%)   <- genuinely varies
```

Where Edison names SL-10, 1 ml/L is strongly evidenced. But that is a population
statistic applied to an individual record — exactly what the template forbids the
model from doing — so it stays **curator evidence, not an auto-apply**.

A 106-record deduplicated batch is running in the background (resumable; the runner
skips completed records). Outputs land in gitignored `research/media/`.

## The invariant-volume shortcut does not hold — tested and recorded (PR #251)

I proposed reusing a stock's usual addition volume for records MediaDive cannot
serve ("SL-10 is 1 ml/L in 36/36 media"). Measured, it fails:

```
Trace element solution SL-10   n=36  1 distinct volume   invariant — matches 0 blocked records
Seven vitamins solution        n=48  4 distinct volumes  matches 87 blocked records
Trace salt solution            n=3   1 distinct volume   "invariant" at n=3
```

The well-sampled stocks vary; the ones that look invariant are under-sampled. There
is no stock where the argument is both strong and applicable.

The cause is a **selection effect**: SL-10 is a DSMZ stock, DSMZ media are exactly
what MediaDive serves, so every SL-10 user was already repaired in #243/#245. The
blocked records are blocked *because* they are non-DSMZ, and they use other stocks —
their SL-10 name matches carry quite different values (MnCl2 5.1 vs SL-10's 0.1).

## What shipped instead

`just identify-cocktail-stocks` names the stock for **190 of the 315** blocked
records, by the same name+value agreement the applier requires (≥3 components):

| stock | records | observed n | modal volume |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| Seven vitamins solution | 87 | 48 | 1 ml (92%) |
| Trace salt solution | 54 | 3 | 1 ml (100%, n=3) |
| Wolfe's mineral elixir | 15 | 12 | 1 ml (83%) |

The volume distribution is reported as evidence and deliberately **not** applied; a
test asserts no column can imply a chosen volume, and another keeps the negative
finding in the docstring so the shortcut is not re-proposed.

This converts "unknown stock, unknown volume" into "known stock, volume to confirm"
for 190 records at once — the state a curator can finish from, versus the Edison
lane's ~12% hit rate one record at a time.

**Status of the remaining 315:** 190 stock-identified (volume needed), 125 not
identified. The Edison batch is stopped at 20/106 on a `402 Payment Required` from
the Edison account — resumable if credits are restored, though at ~12% yield it
would unblock roughly 10 more records.

## Claude research path used while Edison is out of credit — 54 more nested (PR #252)

Edison has returned `402 Payment Required` since 2026-08-08, so this used the native
path the repo already documents in `.claude/skills/deep-research-medium/SKILL.md`:
render the prompt with `just validate-media-recipe --template
templates/media_stock_solution_research.md`, then research it with the harness's web
tools.

**Target chosen by impact.** #251 had already identified 54 blocked records as using
"Trace salt solution" but could not supply its volume — so one research question
unblocked all 54.

**Both facts read from the primary source.** DSMZ medium 84: *"Trace element
solution: FeSO4 x 7 H2O 0.1 g / MnCl2 x 4 H2O 0.1 g / ZnSO4 x 7 H2O 0.1 g /
Distilled water 100.0 ml"*, used as *"Trace element solution (see below) 1.0 ml"* per
1000 ml. The 54 records carry exactly those three salts at 1 G_PER_L — the stock
strength. The volume was then confirmed in **each citing medium's own sheet**, not
carried across: 252 *"(see medium 84) 1.0 ml"*, 993 *"Trace salts solution (see
medium 84) 1"*, 547 *"Trace salt solution 1"*.

This is **not** the shortcut #251 rejected. That was a population-modal volume, which
fails because well-sampled stocks vary and invariant-looking ones are under-sampled
("Trace salt solution" was n=3 there). Here the number is printed in the source;
MediaDive agreeing is corroboration, not the basis.

| metric | original | now |
|---|--:|--:|
| implausible rows | 11,540 | **10,359** |
| flattened cocktails | 579 | **305** (274 repaired, **47%**) |

New tracked `data/import_tracking/researched_stock_volumes.json` carries researched
stocks with citations; `--use-researched` consults it only where MediaDive returned
nothing, and every move still passes the name+value test.

Two bugs caught before shipping: the nested solution claimed *"volume from
MediaDive"* for researched stocks (now cites the DSMZ PDF), and CI caught a stale
derived-artifacts manifest that local missed — the manifest reads `git ls-files`, so
a newly added artifact is invisible until it is committed.

## "Seven vitamins solution" researched — and my 87-record projection was wrong (PR #253)

**The research is solid.** DSMZ medium 503 states "Seven vitamins solution 1.00 ml";
medium 504 reproduces the stock in full. All 40 media citing it among the blocked
records were fetched: 26 state the volume in their own sheet and **all 26 say 1.00
ml** — none contradicted it. The other 14 are lettered variants (298b-i, 503b/c,
829a) whose PDFs 404.

**It forced a new safety gate.** MediaDive observes this stock at four different
volumes corpus-wide, so a volume belongs to the *citing medium*, not the stock.
Researched entries now carry `applies_to_media`; a record whose medium was never read
is left alone rather than inheriting a volume by association.

**But it unlocks 1 record, not 87.** I projected otherwise and was wrong. Those 87
have their *vitamin* stock identified — they are blocked by their **other** stock. The
dominant unmatched row is `FeCl2 x 4 H2O` at 1.5 (63 records); I assumed SL-10, and it
is not — `halosimplex_medium` carries H3BO3 at 3 where SL-10 has 0.006, a 500x
difference. Those media use other, unresearched trace stocks, and the refuse-partial
guard correctly declines to half-repair them.

### Revised view of the remaining 304

The remainder is a **long tail of per-stock research**, not a few more questions. Each
distinct trace stock needs its own source read, and most unlock only a handful of
records. The two stocks done so far (Trace salt, Seven vitamins) were the
concentrated cases.

| metric | original | now |
|---|--:|--:|
| implausible rows | 11,540 | **10,355** |
| flattened cocktails | 579 | **304** (275 repaired, **47%**) |

The Seven-vitamins entry remains a permanent asset: those 87 records unlock the
moment their co-occurring trace stock is researched.

## JCM media are reachable after all — my own code was blocking them (PR #254)

I twice concluded in this issue that MediaDive does not serve JCM media. **That was
wrong, and the block was in `mediadive_id()`**, which matched only
`mediadive.medium:<digits>` and excluded the `J` form — with a test asserting
`J390` must be rejected. The premise came from sampling three ids (J390, J773, C96)
that simply do not exist.

Direct probing, since confirmed by a deep-research pass:

```
DSMZ_MediumJ58.pdf            404   <- PDF sheets really do stop at DSMZ numbers
rest/medium/J58               200   with solutions[]
rest/medium-composition/J58   200   (but see below — wrong endpoint)
jcm.riken.jp GRMD=58          200   (GRMD=390 is the empty page)
```

25 of 25 sampled J-ids from this corpus resolve with `solutions[]`, exposing the same
`{"solution": ..., "amount": 1, "unit": "ml"}` reference the repair already reads.

**Result:** 70 blocked cocktails carried J-ids the fetcher skipped outright. Coverage
rose 186 -> 249 resolvable; **24 nested from each medium's OWN recipe** — no
cross-medium inference.

| metric | original | now |
|---|--:|--:|
| implausible rows | 11,540 | **10,244** |
| flattened cocktails | 579 | **279** (300 repaired, **52%**) |

### Research findings worth recording

- **`J<n>` == `GRMD=<n>`, identity mapping.** Verified across all 1,313 MediaDive JCM
  records: the `link` field is `jcm_grmd?GRMD=<n>` and the integer matches the id in
  every case, 0 mismatches. Corroborated independently against RIKEN pages.
- **`/rest/medium-composition/` is the wrong endpoint** — by design a flat list with
  no solution attribution and no addition volume. `/rest/medium/` is the one to use
  (which is what the fetcher does).
- **Licensing is clean for our use:** MediaDive data, including the JCM import JCM
  explicitly permitted DSMZ to publish, is **CC BY 4.0** — citation required. RIKEN's
  own JCM website is all-rights-reserved, so scraping GRMD pages directly would be a
  different legal footing. We consume MediaDive, so we are fine, but that is worth
  knowing before anyone adds a JCM scraper.
- **Caveats:** the JCM subset is a frozen 2022 semi-automatic import (still exactly
  1,313 records), ~12-15% of linked GRMD pages are now dead, and **~19% of
  multi-solution J-media carry orphan solutions with no addition volume at all** —
  consistent with the "resolved but no cocktail stock" skips seen here.

### Two other fixes in the same PR
- **Full stock signatures.** The audit flags trace salts at >=1 g/l, so only SL-10's
  FeCl2 is ever flagged; flag-based matching found 0 SL-10 records while
  full-composition matching finds 105. `match_stock_signature` moves the whole stock
  rather than the flagged fragment.
- **The #244 trap in my own gate.** `source_medium` trusted the notes' "DSMZ Medium:
  N" stamp, but on a KOMODO record N is the KOMODO id — KOMODO 294 is DSMZ 294 =
  SYNTROPHUS HQGo1, a different medium. Only `mediadive.medium:` ids are trusted now.

2026-08-25 media-content remediation update (branch codex/media-content-remediation-2026-08-25): fresh audit is now 9,688 implausible rows across 3,516 records and 183 flattened cocktails. This branch removes 69 source-backed row findings and three cocktails from the immediately preceding 9,757 / 186 baseline, then lowers both Justfile and test ratchets to 9,688 / 183. The remaining 183 are still source/volume curation; no modal or customary addition volume was inferred.

Current state after #349: the broad plausibility backlog is 9,688 findings across 3,516 records, and the structural `flattened_stock_cocktail` queue is 183 records (down from 186 immediately before this remediation; the older 579 count in the issue body is no longer current). The remediation fixed only three cocktails and 69 findings for which preserved source evidence supplied final concentrations or stock-addition volumes. The remaining 183 are not mechanically safe: each needs an authoritative stock identity plus an evidenced addition volume before nesting. Canonical worklist: `data/import_tracking/reports/concentration_plausibility_by_record.tsv`; ratchets now pin 9,688 total findings and 183 cocktails. This remains open as source-backed batch curation, with no defensible automatic value promotion available in #349.

Local, **uncommitted** follow-up on concentration curation and its audit trail:

The cumulative source-specific audit now passes after fixing two stale-history
tests. Their follow-up list stopped before later applied stock/variant repairs.
The tests now share the cumulative auditor's registry and independently validate
each repair before checking historical claims. Recomputing a hash cannot approve
a forged ingredient or rewritten history; those negative tests fail as intended.

Current cumulative accounting is 5,134 edited records, 1,404 quantity corrections,
585 stock-node relocations and 419 unsupported quantity slots withdrawn with
source-backed context retained. The 31,168 evidence entries also cover batch,
preparation and relationship claims; they are **not** a count of verified
final-medium concentrations or completion of this issue.

This latest pass corrects only two evidence excerpts, adding no concentration
values. The official-source reference-validator repair is documented in #571:
all 206 excerpts and 19 titles in the seven-record cohort now pass. The remaining
91 M142-dependent records are still unapplied. Original JCM670 has been inspected
for M689: four stock additions are explicitly per liter, whereas the import
stores them as g/L. That repair is still pending, including its stock definitions
and the separate treatment of batch masses versus final concentrations.

The full all-record review, remaining source/data conflicts, publication gates,
and requested PR/merge workflow remain open. This update does not close #150.

title: Corpus repair for the implausible-concentration audit (unfinished half of #118)
